{{Quote|After all, the Republic is really to blame for all of our Galaxy's struggles. A Confederacy of Independent Systems is in the making&mdash;and a great galactic war is inevitable.|[[San Hill/Legends|San Hill]]|<ref name="Eyes">{{StoryCite|story=The Eyes of Revolution|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}</ref>}}
The '''Separatist Crisis''' ([[24 BBY/Legends|24 BBY]]&ndash;[[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]) was the two year long [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] Cold War that began eight years after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], characterized by the secession of several thousand [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] to form the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], led by the charismatic ex-[[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Count of Serenno/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]]. The period was marked by growing violence between Separatist- and Republic-supporting factions, the displacement of many billions of [[Refugee/Legends|refugees]], and intense debate on the issue of [[Military Creation Act/Legends|restoring]] a centralized [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] to counter the perceived threat from the CIS.

The crisis came to a head in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], when a [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi-led]] investigation of an [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|assassination attempt]] on [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] linked various megacorporations, including the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]], [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]], and [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] to the Separatist movement. Gathering evidence that these corporations were planning to pool their [[Droid Army|droid armies]] to overwhelm the Republic, the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] granted [[Emergency Powers Act/Legends|emergency powers]] to [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], who used them to acquire a [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|clone army]] from [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] and launch a [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|pre-emptive strike]] on the [[Geonosis droid factories/Legends|droid foundries]] of [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], beginning the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-spanning [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

The crisis was ultimately discovered to have been manipulated and intensified by [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] and alter ego of Supreme Chancellor Palpatine, who worked with Dooku to lay the groundwork for a war that would bring about the culmination of the [[Order of the Sith Lords|Sith]] [[Grand Plan/Legends|Grand Plan]] to [[Order 66/Legends|destroy]] the Jedi Order and transform the Republic into the Sith-led [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].

==Prelude==
===Political factors===
{{Quote|Pay heed to the way the Republic and the Jedi Order deal with them. The Federation will be dismantled, and the precedent will be set. Unless you take steps to begin a slow, carefully planned withdrawal from the Senate, taking your home and client systems with you, you, too, risk becoming the property of the Republic.|Dark Lord of the Sith [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]] to a holo-audience of the [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]], the [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]], and the [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]], on how the Republic had dealt with the Trade Federation upon enacting the blockade of Naboo to protect its interests|<ref name="Darth Plagueis (novel)">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>}}
Although the Republic provided some measure of political unity, and promoted a norm of negotiation, it lacked a military force capable of maintaining order. Security was the province of individual [[Planet/Legends|planets]], or powerful interplanetary blocs like the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]]. Thus, there was a kind of latent anarchy beneath the civilized surface. The planets that would later constitute the Confederacy of Independent Systems (CIS) brought this deficit into plain sight by departing from the Republic.

Although it is not entirely clear, there might have been reasons for both weak and strong planets to follow this course of action. Strong planets obviously would fare well under a more decentralized regime, because they could exercise their power openly. But while the Republic's influence may have been enough to thus irritate the great powers, it was not enough to convince the weaker powers that it could truly protect them, as the [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] crisis demonstrated. Perhaps smaller-scale alliances would provide better protection than a commitment to a galactic government.

A surging sense of Outer Rim nationalism in the final decades of the Republic also informed the desire for secession and for the later creation of the CIS. Many star systems in the Middle and Outer felt exploited and ignored, and calls for unity under an independent government began to greatly increase as it appeared that the Republic was beyond fixing. 

===Economic factors===
{{Quote|There will come a time when that cult of greed, called the Republic, will lose all pretext of democracy and freedom.|Dooku|<ref name="The Clone Wars Campaign Guide">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref>}}
Advocates of decentralization also found support amongst the free-trade lobby. A galactic government could either impose its own taxes, adding to trade barriers put in place by planets, or favor a liberal trade regime, compelling planets to lower those barriers. The Republic tended towards the former model, in part perhaps because it lacked the power to pursue the latter. It thus became much resented by business and trade actors. The CIS offered an alternative of the liberalizing but otherwise minimalist governance that these actors found attractive.

==The Crisis==
===The Raxus Address===
{{Quote|I will not let this Republic that has stood for a thousand years be split in two. My negotiations will not fail.|[[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]|<ref name="EpII">{{Film|II}}</ref>}}
The Confederacy of Independent Systems began in [[24 BBY/Legends|24 BBY]] when, after eight years in seclusion, Count Dooku commandeered a Republic communications station in the [[Tion Hegemony/Legends|Tion Hegemony]] and delivered an [[Raxus Address/Legends|address]] from [[Raxus Prime/Legends|Raxus Prime]], denouncing the Senate and the Jedi for allowing the Republic's ideals and morals to decline.<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

The [[Raxus Address/Legends|Raxus Address]] set off a wave of secessions: for decades, numerous planets, species, and groups had been trying to reduce the power of the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], lower or eliminate taxes, grant graft in exchange for political favors, or withdraw from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] for various isolationist or xenophobic reasons. Spurred by the disillusioned Dooku and the failure of the Senate to even vote on the [[Financial Reform Act]], the various corporations and planets began to withdraw from the Senate in 24 BBY, organizing themselves into the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].

For all its effect on [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], the CIS was really more of a movement than an organized state. It ultimately became a loosely-organized affiliation of various megacorps and planets with a wide range of ambitions and philosophies. Some sought for the new CIS to destroy the Republic, but many others simply wanted local independence and had little enthusiasm for a new centralized government. This resulted in a loose [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|confederation]] which saw the megacorporations seated on the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] owing to their military and economic power, overriding the authority of the democratic [[Separatist Senate/Legends|Separatist Parliament]] and allowing for capitalism with no government involvement in planetary affairs.<ref name="Warfare" />

In public, Dooku swayed planets and commercial concerns to his side while privately training a number of [[Dark side adept/Legends|Dark Side Adepts]], including [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]], [[Sev'rance Tann/Legends|Sev'rance Tann]], and [[Saato]]. Other soldiers who sided with the Confederacy included the [[Gen'Dai/Legends|Gen'Dai]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Durge/Legends|Durge]], [[Cydon Prax]], and [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], a [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] rebuilt as a [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] warrior by the IG Banking Clan, who would become the [[Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies/Legends|Supreme Commander of the Droid Armies]].<ref name="NEC" />

The crisis began at the end of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] eight years in office. Palpatine was [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|constitutionally]]-obliged to step down that year, but exactly as Darth Sidious had planned, the Senate voted to allow him an indefinite extension of his term until the threat was resolved. Amidst much debate, he agreed to allow discussion of a [[Military Creation Act/Legends|Military Creation Act]] that would restore the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] to counter the threat of separatism.<ref name="NEC" />

===The Confederacy takes shape===
The year 24 BBY saw thousands of planets leave the Republic, with multiple planets leaving every day. Many Senators believed that the Confederacy should be allowed to exist alongside the Republic, while others pushed for the passage of the [[Military Creation Act/Legends|Military Creation Act]] to bolster the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]].<ref name="NEC" />

[[File:SecessionistMovement.png|thumb|left|200px|The Separatist leadership on Geonosis.]]
Dooku's emerging [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] secretly used the negotiation period to begin building droid armies, in the hope that by the time negotiations invariably failed, they would be strong enough to force the Republic to grant them independence anyway. Dooku secretly solicited help from the galaxy's six major industrial powers, and while none of them declared for the CIS until the very start of the Clone Wars, their financial assistance was of invaluable help to Dooku. On [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]], [[Baktoid Armor Workshop/Legends|Baktoid Armor Workshop's]] [[Geonosis droid factories/Legends|droid foundries]] produced thousands of [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]]. The [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] of [[Muunilinst/Legends|Muunilinst]], led by [[San Hill/Legends|San Hill]], provided both loans and [[IG-227 Hailfire-class droid tank/Legends|Hailfire droid tanks]] and [[IG lancer droid/Legends|IG lancer combat droids]] from its [[Collections and Security Division/Legends|Collections and Security Division]]. The [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]] led by [[Gossam/Legends|Gossam]] magistrate [[Shu Mai/Legends|Shu Mai]] provided raw materials. [[Wat Tambor/Legends|Wat Tambor's]] [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] provided dozens of [[Factory world/Legends|factory worlds]], forming a region of space that became known as the "[[Foundry of the Confederacy/Legends|Foundry of the Confederacy]]." A quieter backer was [[Passel Argente/Legends|Passel Argente's]] [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]], which regulated the distribution of retail products.<ref name="NEC" /><ref name="Warfare" />

Despite four trials in the [[Supreme Court/Legends|Supreme Court]] for his command of the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invasion of Naboo]], [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] remained the [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Viceroy]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]]. Unaware that his former backer, [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], was now backing the Separatists, Gunray went to Count Dooku and told him everything he knew about the shadowy [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] who claimed to control the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]. Dooku, who had already sworn himself to Sidious as Darth Tyranus, accepted Gunray's account. Gunray's price for the support of the Trade Federation and its [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|droid army]] was the death of [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], in revenge for his humiliation ten years earlier.<ref name="EpII" />

While Supreme Chancellor Palpatine vowed that he would never allow the Republic to be split in two, he did not publicly support the creation of a Republic Military, and the Senate vote on the Military Creation Act was delayed endlessly.<ref name="NEC" /> This led many Separatists to gleefully regard Palpatine as a lightweight, adept at maintaining power but incapable of formulating a coherent response to the Republic's many secessionist movements.<ref name="Author's Cut 8">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 8: Tales of the Clone Wars}}</ref> 

Once these secessionists gain strength and numbers, expressions of discontent escalate. Attacks on Republic facilities become common. Senators are threatened or assaulted.<ref name="The Clone Wars Campaign Guide">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

===Antar 4===
{{Main|Battle of Antar 4 (Separatist Crisis)}}
A major turning point in the crisis was the [[Battle of Antar 4 (Separatist Crisis)|Battle of Antar 4]], which occurred in [[23 BBY/Legends|22.5 BBY]]. The botched Republic attempt to remove a radical, Separatist-affiliated terrorist government from [[Antar 4/Legends|Antar 4]] not only resulted in converting the majority of Antar 4's citizens' sympathies to the Separatists, but also showed Separatist-leaning worlds that the Republic was not as infallible as had been thought.<ref name="NEC" />

In the eighteen months prior to the Battle of Antar 4, over a thousand worlds had joined the Confederacy but violence had been generally limited. During the [[New Year Fete Week/Legends|New Year Fete Week]] on Antar 4, however, the [[Roshu Sune/Legends|Roshu Sune]], the militant splinter branch of the [[Gotal Assembly for Separation/Legends|Gotal Assembly for Separation]], activated the sleeper agents they had placed within the chapter houses of the Jedi-allied [[Antarian Rangers/Legends|Antarian Rangers]]. The moon was thrown into chaos as the Rangers were decimated, and the Roshu Sune issued a declaration of secession.<ref name="NEC" />

Antarian Rangers from across the galaxy descended on Antar 4 looking for revenge, while a Jedi task force led by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Masters]] [[Saesee Tiin/Legends|Saesee Tiin]] and [[Coleman Trebor/Legends|Coleman Trebor]] spearheaded the Republic's response. However, the first assault was a disaster, with heavy Jedi and civilian casualties. The Jedi ultimately resorted to using an [[Electromagnetic pulse/Legends|electromagnetic pulse]] to overwhelm the [[Gotal/Legends|Gotals']] sensitive head cones, but at the cost of causing severe pain and incapacitation to the civilian Gotal population. The sloppy tactics cost the Republic considerable goodwill on Antar 4, while Separatist-leaning planets took heart from the realization that the Republic was not unbeatable.<ref name="NEC" />

The [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] refused to trace any connection between the Roshu Shune and Count Dooku, an ex-Jedi, even as random terrorist bombings began striking Coruscant. Dooku himself did not condemn the killings being done in his name.

===Splintering of the Republic===
Three months prior to the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]], the planets [[Ando/Legends|Ando]] and [[Sy Myrthian/Legends|Sy Myrth]] seceded. The [[Ando separation]] was for many a microcosm of the the greater galactic conflict when the [[Aqualish/Legends|Aqualish]] of the [[Andoan Free Colonies/Legends|Andoan Free Colonies]] refused to acknowledge the Ando-based [[Spiverelda/Legends|Spiverelda]] government's declaration of secession. The twin secessions brought the total of Separatist planets to over six thousand.<ref name="NEC" />

Another notable point in the Separatist Crisis was the [[Border dispute on Ansion/Legends|Ansion border dispute]], in which the [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]] tried to get the people of Ansion to withdraw from the Republic, which would have meant other more important planets would withdraw due to Ansion's numerous treaties with neighboring planets.

The [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] sent four Jedi ([[Luminara Unduli/Legends|Luminara Unduli]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Barriss Offee/Legends|Barriss Offee]]) to try and keep Ansion within the Republic. In the end they managed to call a truce between the pro-Secession [[Unity Council]] and the nomad [[Alwari]], the dispute between the Unity Council and the Alwari tribes was being used by the Commerce Guild and the Ansionion Senator [[Mousul]] to convince the Ansionions they would be benefit more from being out of the Republic.

However, after the Jedi managed to form a truce between the two sides the Ansionions decided they did not need to leave the Republic after all and overwhelmingly voted against secession.

The failure of Ansion meant that the Separatists were delayed from issuing demands to the Republic, but Dooku only considered Ansion to be a minor setback.

The Separatist Crisis ended when the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]] began.
